views.markdown: Adjust brightness and extra dimming with the same Control Center slider. Above your chosen threshold, it controls normal brightness. Below it, Apple's native Reduce White Point dims the screen further while brightness stays at minimum.

views.markdown: Screenshots and illustrations from Jonas Schiefner's original project. The current Settings pane may differ.

Start with the default 30% split, or open **AdvancedBrightnessSlider Continued** in Settings and adjust **Threshold**. Threshold changes apply automatically.

The Settings pane requires **PreferenceLoader** and **Cephei Tweak Support**. This package replaces the original AdvancedBrightnessSlider and retains existing preferences.
Originally developed by **Jonas Schiefner**. Independently maintained by **0chium**, with compatibility updates for the specific builds listed in Compatibility. Free and GPL-3.0 licensed.

**iPhone 14 Pro** — iOS 17.0 (21A329): owner reports working brightness mapping and threshold preferences.

**iPhone 11 Pro Max** — iOS 18.3.2 (22D82): owner reports functional success and successful Sileo replacement of the earlier package, preserving the threshold.

**iPhone SE (2nd generation)** — iOS 26.0.1 (23A355): owner reports working brightness mapping with the tested iOS 26 adapter. The Threshold slider’s numeric value is not visible in Settings.

The iOS 17.0 and 18.3.2 reports used earlier candidates. The iOS 26.0.1 report used 1.2.2-1+abs26exp.1; 1.2.3-1 reuses its complete installed payload unchanged. These results cover the listed configurations, not every iOS version or device.

**iPhone SE (2nd generation), iOS 18.2 (22C152):** statically inspected but runtime untested for this update.

**iOS 16:** legacy path retained; the rebuilt continued release is not runtime validated there.

Other modern builds, including other iOS 26 versions, are not enabled. Modern Prysm/BigSurCenter configurations are not claimed as supported.

- Auto-Brightness suppression retains the existing implementation; native-service effectiveness is not independently verified.
- Accessibility White Point changes may affect the screen without repositioning Control Center.
- Controlled disablement conditionally restores borrowed settings only while ownership remains uncontested. Crash, SpringBoard restart or removal cannot guarantee cleanup; system settings may remain changed.
- Startup brightness is not restored.
- On iOS 26.0.1, Settings does not show the Threshold slider’s numeric value.
- iOS 26.0.1 preview isolation has not received a separate focused device test.

Adds iOS 26.0.1 using the adapter tested on iPhone SE (2nd generation). Reuses the tested package’s installed binaries and resources without recompilation. Existing brightness mapping, preferences and credits are preserved.

Original AdvancedBrightnessSlider and presentation assets: **Jonas Schiefner**. Continued compatibility maintenance: **0chium**. Original GPL-3.0 licensing, copyright notices and upstream credits are retained.

Original credits include opa334 / WhitePointModule, rpetrich / Flipswitch, PoomSmart and zaneh.
The donation link above belongs to the original developer, Jonas Schiefner. It has not been redirected to the compatibility maintainer. Donations are optional; the tweak remains free.
